items.title: Carmen Lundy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 15, 2023
items.q: if you ever heard Don Pullen, with Adams and Danny Richmond

ctx.x: Working with all those established piano players must have increased your already developed hearing because Don Pullen is not going to play all the same changes that Walter Bishop Junior is even though the tune may be the same. Did you find that you followed them when they went to different places or did you try to like just stick to what you knew?

This is, you know jazz is such a wonderful experiment where we’re exploring possibilities all the time. It’s the nature of the music you know. And I’m young and I’m anxious and I’m learning and I want to be liked, I want to be known and recognized for being a musician not just a singer myself you see and that little arranging part, there’s something so wonderful and diplomatic and democratic about the experience of this music and to stay open to the possibilities. And you think you might be on this certain track…

about singers yet, okay? We haven’t even talked about the Ellas and the Sarahs and the Carmen McRaes and the Bettys and all that. Okay? This is just how the music — I think I was a sponge, I think I still am. I was just absorbing from the masterful, from the masters really, of that time. I’m in my early twenties and they are fully realized artists at that time in their careers. And I’m just really taking whatever they offer and happy to be in the mix.
